key_insight: A PPO-based controller can coordinate battery, hydrogen, diesel, and grid flows in a community microgrid to preserve high renewable usage and reliability under uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical decision-making layer for hybrid energy systems, helping operators balance cost, emissions, and resilience in real time.
method: Formulated the microgrid as an MDP with 11 state variables and 3 continuous actions.
Used PPO to dispatch battery, diesel, and hydrogen storage while computing grid exchange from remaining power balance.
Evaluated performance on an 8,760-hour simulation for a 1,000-household community in Rockhampton, Australia.
evidence_signal: In the normal case, the EMS achieved A$195,690.67 annual revenue, 91.2% renewable fraction, 0.085 kg CO2/kWh carbon intensity, and 99.77% load satisfaction; under higher outage probability, it still met 98.79% of demand.
watch_item: Results may be sensitive to renewable variability, training stability, and the specific accounting boundary used for emissions and performance.
paper_title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Energy Management for Hydrogen-Enabled Community Microgrids Under Uncertainty
